chunks: Uyun al-Akhbar: Via his three chains (which taken collectively lend credence to the report) from al-Fadhl b. Shadhan from al-Ridha (peace be upon him) in his letter to al-Ma'mun:

… and that it (i.e. the Truthful Book) is True, all of it, from its Opening to its Conclusion. We believe in its Muhkam (clear verses) and its Mutashabih (ambiguous), its Khass (specific) and its Amm (general), its Wa'd (promise) and its Wa'id (threat), its Nasikh (abrogating) and its Mansukh (abrogated), its Qasas (stories) and its Akhbar (reports)
ai.seo_question: What categories of Quranic verses are considered true and worthy of belief in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Ayn al-Akhbar* via al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, this hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) to Caliph al-Ma'mun serves as a definitive Shia response to theological debates on the Quran's completeness, affirming that every category of verse—whether *muhkam* (clear), *mutashabih* (ambiguous), *naskh* (abrogating), or *mansukh* (abrogated)—is equally true and divinely inspired. This comprehensive acceptance underscores the Shia doctrine that no part of the Quran is false or erroneous, reinforcing the unity of its message across all interpretive layers.

en.ammaar-muslim: [1/1577] Uyun al-Akhbar: Via his three chains (which taken collectively lend credence to the report) from al-Fadhl b. Shadhan from al-Ridha عليه السلام in his letter to al-Ma’mun:

… and that it (i.e. the Truthful Book) is True, all of it, from its Opening to its Conclusion. We believe in its Muhkam (clear verses) and its Mutashabih (ambiguous), its Khass (specific) and its Amm (general), its Wa’d (promise) and its Wa’id (threat), its Nasikh (abrogating) and its Mansukh (abrogated), its Qasas (stories) and its Akhbar (reports)
